mainTopic: Whether a נזיר's unassigned animals count as 'specified' for particular קרבנות, and why bird offerings and the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל may be special cases
overview: On this amud, רב פפא challenges the view that an animal set aside without being assigned is not treated as 'specified' (מפורשת) for a particular offering. He points to a משנה where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules on a נזיר who brought three animals without saying which is for which offering. Each animal may still be offered as the קרבן it fits: חטאת, עולה, or שלמים. רב שימי בר אשי answers that bird offerings are a special case. The verses 'ולקח' and 'ועשה' teach that birds get their assignment either when the owner takes them (לקיחת בעלים) or when the כהן offers them (עשיית כהן). So the birds tell us nothing about animals in general. He then begins to explain that the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is also a special exception ('הכא נמי'), and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the three unassigned animals of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רב שימי בר אשי using the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A נזיר who brought three animals without assigning them may still offer each as the offering it fits. That seems to show animals do count as specified.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to your reasoning, look at the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if a person brought three animals and did not say which is which, each one is offered as the offering it fits: חטאת, עולה, or שלמים. Why should that work? You said an animal is not treated as specified!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the other side's view that an animal is not considered 'specified' for a particular offering. He quotes a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other side holds that animals set aside without assigning them are not locked into specific offerings. Yet רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets each animal go to the offering it naturally fits, as though each were already assigned. So רב פפא asks how that can work if animals are 'not specified'.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: used to turn the other person's logic back against him
And he did not specify which animal is for which offering
The one that is fit for a certain offering
It is treated as specified, already assigned to a particular offering

steps.confusionAlert: Each of a נזיר's three offerings needs a different kind of animal. That is why each unassigned animal can 'fit' only one of them: the female lamb fits the חטאת, the male lamb fits the עולה, and the ram fits the שלמים.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא speaking to רב שימי בר אשי.

phrases.english: that which we learned in a mishna:
If he brought three animals and did not specify,
the one fit for a sin-offering is sacrificed as a sin-offering,
the one fit for a burnt-offering is sacrificed as a burnt-offering,
the one fit for a peace-offering is sacrificed as a peace-offering.
an animal is not considered as specified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion before this section by challenging the other side's position that animals are not 'specified'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an animal set aside without assigning it is not treated as specified (בהמה לאו כמפורשת דמיא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets each unassigned animal be offered as the קרבן it fits. That treats the animals as already specified, which contradicts the claim.

steps.title: Bird offerings are special because of the verses 'and he shall take' and 'and he shall sacrifice'
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי answers that bird offerings are a special case. The תורה says their assignment can happen either when the owner takes them or when the כהן offers them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, the verses say 'and he shall take... and he shall sacrifice.' The Merciful One is saying the birds can be assigned either when the owner takes them or when the כהן offers them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי begins his defense. He explains that the birds are a special exception because of what the verses say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses about bird offerings use two verbs: 'ולקח' (the owner takes) and 'ועשה' (the כהן offers). From this we learn that the birds can be assigned at either moment. That rule comes from the verses, so it does not prove anything about animals in general.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One: a name for G-d or the תורה
The owner's taking (buying or acquiring) of the offering
The כהן's doing, meaning his offering it on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that bird offerings (קינין) can get their assignment as late as when the כהן offers them. The גמרא uses that idea to block proofs drawn from birds.

phrases.notes: Now רב שימי בר אשי answers. 'There' means the case of bird offerings.

phrases.english: "And he shall take ... and he shall sacrifice."
either by the taking of the owner,
or by the action of the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the defense against רב פפא's challenge by showing that bird offerings are a special case based on the verses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case exception based on a verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since bird offerings can wait to be assigned until the כהן offers them, you might think this shows a general rule for all offerings, animals included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Birds are a special case because the verses allow them to be assigned at the owner's taking or at the כהן's offering. This tells us nothing about animals in general.

steps.title: Starting to explain why the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is also special
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי begins to say that the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is likewise a special case. The text stops mid-sentence.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב שימי בר אשי is about to explain why the three animals of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are also a special exception, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכא נמי' signals that he will treat רב פפא's case the same way he treated the birds. It too is a special exception, so it does not disprove the rule that animals are not treated as specified. The actual reason has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: applying the same idea to the current case

phrases.notes: 'Here' means the three animals in the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the special-case approach from the birds and begins applying it to the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case exception (explanation continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to show that all animals count as specified.
steps.terutzMaskana: That case is also a special exception. The reason is given in the continuation.
